messages:
eval-bot: nightly-eval alert: customer-support promptset failure rate increased by 3.2x vs baseline. see dashboard -> https://redwood-ci/runs/1912345 :rotating_light:

mira: ugh. noticed any config changes last night?

sam: rolling change to cache sharding landed last night (shard-count -> 128, shard-salt enabled). i thought it was safe but report looks correlated with deploy window.

alex: i grabbed two failing examples, same prompt, same model/version, different runs -> tokens diverge at step 12. putting side-by-side:
```
# run A
User: How do I reset my password?
Assistant: You can reset your password by going to Settings -> Security... [continues]
# run B
User: How do I reset my password?
Assistant: To change your password, visit account settings, then select "Password". If you can't, contact support... [differs]
```

alex: seems like cache prefix lookup sometimes returns a prefix generated from another tenant when shards collide. not 100% yet.

jin: repro script i used:
```
CACHE_SHARDS=128 ./scripts/repro_prefix_collision.sh --promptset customer-support --runs 10
```

jin: log extract shows two keys mapping to same shorthash after truncation: `kv_prefix:sha1(tk:tenant:prompt)[:8]` -> both tenants produced `ab12c3f9`

mira: so our key truncation + shard salting can cause collisions across tenants -> stale KV returned -> generation drift. does that match the failures?

sam: makes sense. we optimized key size for mem footprint but didn't account for namespace entropy with more shards. i can see shard-salt exposing different upstream prefixes into same LRU window.

alex: quick check: when i force per-tenant namespace by prepending tenant-id to the hashed input, reproducer stops showing divergence.

jin: proposed mitigations:
- short term: disable shard-salt (rollback) or increase key length from 8->16 hex chars
- medium: include tenant-id in the cache key (tenant-scoped namespace)
- long term: move to keyed LRU per-tenant or probabilistic TTL to avoid reusing foreign kvs

mira: agree. short-term rollback should be fastest. can someone open a rollback PR + a patch to add tenant-id to the key in parallel?

sam: i'll open rollback PR now (link coming). also will add metric to alert on per-prompt key-collision rate (new metric: kv.prefix_collision.count).

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/714 (revert shard-salt). tagging @eng-ml for visibility.

alex: i'll draft a follow-up PR to change key derivation to `sha256(tenant_id || ":" || prompt)[:16]` and add tests for cross-tenant collisions.

jin: local quick patch i ran (python snippet):
```
def cache_key(tenant, prompt):
    import hashlib
    k = tenant + ':' + prompt
    return hashlib.sha256(k.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```

mira: testing plan: run repro script 50x on nightly infra after rollback, compare failure rate, plus run canary on 5% of traffic with new key derivation. if stable, roll to 100%.

eval-bot: triggered nightly repro job (job id 1912346-repro-1). will post summary when complete.

sam: thanks. once rollback merged i'll coordinate canary window and dashboards to watch: promptset failure rate, avg latency, kv.hit_ratio, kv.prefix_collision.count.

alex: noted. i'll add unit test that simulates 10k tenants to ensure collision rate is negligible with new key length.

mira: great work. let's keep thread for updates only. if someone hits a blocker ping here. :thumbsup:
